newsitem.title: USA: U.S. will back lifting sanctions on Serbia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. will back lifting sanctions on Serbia.

text.p: The United States said on Monday, after Bosnia's three-man presidency held their first post-election meeting in Sarajevo, that it would support lifting sanctions against the rump Yugoslavia.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters the U.N. Security Council would "very quickly" consider resolution 1022, on lifting sanctions suspended after last year's Dayton accords.
"It will be formally lifted I think just in a matter of days. The United States will support this because it meets the criteria that we helped to negotiate at Dayton," Burns said.
Sanctions against the Yugoslav state comprising Serbia and Montenegro were suspended by the council last November as a follow-up to the U.S.-initiated Balkan peace accords signed in Dayton, Ohio.
The council's resolution stipulated the sanctions would be lifted entirely 10 days after the Sept. 14 Bosnian elections. Russia insisted that meant Sept. 24.
But Washington viewed the resolution as saying the 10-day countdown should begin after the the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) had certified the elections in writing.
The OSCE certified the poll results on Sunday despite charges of voting irregularities, including one claim that 103 percent of registered voters had cast ballots.
Burns said "it is not at all clear" that the 103 percent claim was true.

He said the certification, coupled with the first meeting of Moslem, Serb and Croat members of the Bosnian presidency, meant the Bosnia peace process was moving forward and the sancitons could be lifted.
